title: Text tool: editing text double-renders (canvas object + overlay, slightly offset) and looks duplicated on double-click — editingTextId never excluded from canvas render
description:
USER-REPORTED (text is core authoring). Two related Text-tool defects on the stage; they SHARE one root cause.

REPRO 1 (create): Select the Text tool, single-click empty stage. A text box opens with the editable value "Text" focused, BUT a SECOND non-editable "Text" renders underneath, slightly offset — two overlapping "Text"s. Expected: only the editable overlay shows; no doubled/offset rendered copy.

REPRO 2 (edit, followup): Double-click an existing on-stage textbox to edit it. It appears DUPLICATED — two text boxes visible. Expected: edit the existing box in place with no second box.

SHARED ROOT CAUSE (file:line):
The object currently being edited is never excluded from the canvas render, so the model text object stays painted on the stage canvas while the HTML <textarea> edit overlay is drawn on top of it — producing the doubled/overlapping "Text" in BOTH create and double-click-edit.
- packages/authoring-ui/src/Shell.tsx:3200 passes editingTextId={editingTextId} into StageArea (value comes from the ui store, set by handleTextPlace via setEditingTextId, useTextHandlers.ts:57; cleared by handleTextEditEnd, useTextHandlers.ts:73).
- packages/authoring-ui/src/StageArea.tsx:1394 destructures it as `editingTextId: _editingTextId` — the underscore marks it UNUSED. It is never referenced again (grep: only the prop decl at :732 and this discard at :1394).
- packages/authoring-ui/src/StageArea.tsx:3353-3360 builds the SceneGraph for the CanvasRenderer from propSceneGraph (or the flat [...shapeDisplayObjects, ...textDisplayObjects, ...bitmapDisplayObjects] fallback) with NO filtering of the object under edit. So the edited text object is always painted.
- The textarea overlay (StageArea.tsx:4447-4504) is positioned at left/top = stageX/stageY (the object's top-left) with `padding:2`, a `1px dashed border`, and `boxSizing:border-box` (lines 4459-4464). Its text-content origin is therefore inset ~3px (border+padding) from the object's top-left, while the canvas paints text on a font baseline — the two origins do not coincide, which is the SOURCE OF THE SLIGHT OFFSET between the overlay text and the still-rendered canvas text.

WHY BUG 2 IS THE SAME ROOT CAUSE (not a duplicate in the model):
- Double-click-to-edit (selection tool: StageArea.tsx:4076-4092; text tool: StageArea.tsx:1944-1951) sets editingId=hitText.id and on blur calls onTextEdit -> handleTextEdit -> updateDisplayObject (core/timeline.ts:1076-1099), which updates the existing id IN PLACE. The create flow with onTextPlace also sets editingId=id (StageArea.tsx:1975) so its blur takes the editingId branch (onTextEdit, update) — it does NOT call onTextCreated. So NO second DisplayObject is inserted into the model in either flow. The "duplicate" the user sees is the still-painted canvas object sitting under the dashed-bordered overlay (which reads as a separate box) — i.e. the exact same un-hidden-render defect as bug 1.
- (Latent, separate: the legacy fallback at StageArea.tsx:1980-1988 sets editingId=null, whose blur DOES call onTextCreated (StageArea.tsx:4476) and would double-insert — but it only runs when onTextPlace is undefined, which is not the live path. Worth a guard but not the reported cause.)

EXPECTED vs ACTUAL:
- Actual: edited text object is painted on the canvas AND under the overlay (offset by border+padding vs baseline) -> two overlapping "Text"s in both create and edit.
- Expected: while textEditState is active, the object whose id === editingTextId is hidden from the canvas render; the overlay exactly covers the object origin/baseline/scale (no offset, no doubling).

REGRESSION VERDICT: LONG-STANDING, not a recent regression. The unused `_editingTextId` discard, the immediate-place create block, and the overlay all originate in commit 4b4e4cf ("initial progress", 2026-06-09) — the feature shipped with the defect. Commit 5e28b9b later extracted the handlers into useTextHandlers.ts verbatim without behavior change.

FIX DIRECTION:
1. Stop discarding editingTextId in StageArea (StageArea.tsx:1394) and use it to EXCLUDE the matching object from the SceneGraph passed to the CanvasRenderer (StageArea.tsx:3353-3360 — filter both the propSceneGraph layers and the flat-array fallback so the object with id===editingTextId is not painted while editing). Also fold in StageArea's local textEditState.editingId (the source of truth inside StageArea) so it works regardless of the prop round-trip.
2. Align the overlay position EXACTLY to the canvas text origin: account for the border(1px)+padding(2px) inset (e.g. offset left/top by -3px, or set border/padding to 0, or match the canvas font baseline metric) so the overlay text sits exactly where the canvas would have painted it — no slight offset. Verify against renderer text drawing (CanvasRenderer text path) for the baseline convention.
3. (Optional hardening) Guard the legacy onTextCreated fallback (StageArea.tsx:1980-1988 / 4473-4494) so it can never double-insert if editingId is null but an object was already placed.

ACCEPTANCE (note: per env, port 1420 e2e was held by another agent; verify via code + targeted run when free): creating text shows exactly one "Text" (the overlay) with no offset copy; double-clicking an existing textbox edits in place with exactly one visible box; the model keyframe gains no extra DisplayObject on edit (assert displayObjects.length unchanged across an edit commit).

Files: packages/authoring-ui/src/StageArea.tsx (1394, 3353-3360, 4447-4504, 1980-1988); packages/authoring-ui/src/Shell.tsx:3200; packages/authoring-ui/src/hooks/useTextHandlers.ts (57, 73); packages/core/src/model/timeline.ts:1076 (reference, correct/no change).
